claims.claim: Individual health is the health of one person: that person's health status and the care they receive. The WHO's founding definition anchors what health status can mean for a single person: a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.
Clinicians (doctors, nurses, and other direct care providers) are concerned with the health of an individual; the clinician's 'patient' is one person.
Population health is the health outcomes of a group of individuals, including the distribution of such outcomes within the group; this working definition was proposed by Kindig and Stoddart (2003).

Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations, and the application of this study to the control of health problems; the epidemiologist's 'patient' is the community.
Epidemiologists describe health events in a group by pattern, meaning occurrence by time, place, and person, and they compare rates, which relate the number of cases to the size of the population.

Assessing a community's health means identifying and analyzing population data by person, place, and time to find actual and potential health problems, where they occur, and which populations are at increased risk.

Community water fluoridation adjusts the amount of fluoride in drinking water to a level recommended for preventing cavities and benefits all members of a community by preventing cavities, reducing oral health disparities, and saving money for everyone.

A group-level intervention can lift the health of individuals within the group, including people who would not have obtained the benefit on their own; this rising-tide connection is the core link between population and individual health.

The U.S. Healthy People program sets 10-year, measurable public health objectives for the nation and tracks progress toward them, an example of setting goals for a whole population rather than for individual patients.

Medicine and public health are partners: clinicians care for individuals one at a time while public health organizes community-level activities, and the 10 Essential Public Health Services describe the public health activities all communities should undertake.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The terms 'population health' and 'public health' are sometimes used interchangeably in casual writing, and population health as a concept has fuzzy boundaries.
positions: Some writers use 'population health' simply to mean the health of any defined group
Kindig and Stoddart note the term was not yet precisely defined and propose the outcomes-plus-distribution definition used in this lesson
Public health as an organized field and profession is a distinct concept covered by a sibling topic
conflictingEvidence.resolution: This lesson uses the Kindig and Stoddart working definition for population health, treats public health as the organized field, and points readers to the sibling topic public-health:foundations:population-health for depth.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The WHO's founding definition of health ('complete' physical, mental and social well-being) has been criticized as unrealistically absolute.
positions: The 1946 WHO definition is aspirational and framing
Critics note that almost no one experiences 'complete' well-being at all times
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents the WHO definition as the founding anchor for what a person's health status can mean, without claiming it describes a typical person's daily experience.
